questions.question_text: Which of the following is a type of V-code?
Adjustment disorders can only occur in response to traumatic events.
V-codes are used to identify factors that influence a person's mental health status but do not qualify as mental disorders.
Somatic symptom disorder primarily involves physical symptoms that cannot be fully explained by a medical condition.
Individuals diagnosed with factitious disorder intentionally produce or feign symptoms to assume the sick role.
Reactive attachment disorder typically occurs in children who have experienced neglect or frequent changes in caregivers.
The presence of a V-code indicates that the individual has a diagnosed mental illness.
Culture-bound syndromes are not recognized in all parts of the world.
Bereavement can sometimes lead to Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood.
Antisocial behavior in children is always indicative of a future diagnosis of a personality disorder.
Relationship problems as a V-code can include issues between parents and children.
Factitious disorder is characterized by experiencing physical symptoms without any external incentive.
V-codes can only be used in the context of clinical diagnoses, not in research settings.
Dissociative disorders involve disruptions in memory, identity, or perception of the environment.
Adjustment disorders can resolve on their own without treatment.
Adult antisocial behavior patterns can include criminal activities but do not always have to do with legal issues.
The diagnosis of a child with conduct disorder is solely based on academic performance.
Individuals with grief and bereavement issues may not meet the criteria for a mental disorder.
Some V-codes may be applicable to individuals without any diagnosed mental health conditions.
The primary focus of treatment for adjustment disorders is typically on coping skills and problem-solving.
Cultural influences play no role in the development of psychological disorders.
Reactive attachment disorder is diagnosed when a child fails to develop appropriate emotional attachments primarily due to inadequate care.
Individuals with somatic symptom disorder often seek medical help for their unexplained physical symptoms.
V-codes can help healthcare providers address concerns that are affecting a patient's mental well-being.
The criteria for a factitious disorder include symptoms that are reliably produced and are inconsistent with any known medical condition.
Relationship problems categorized under V-codes do not impact the overall well-being of individuals significantly.
